newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cable maker Perennial ends debut higher.
newsitem.headline: Cable maker Perennial ends debut higher.

text.p: Shares of cable and wire maker Perennial International Ltd ended their trading debut on Monday at HK$1.19 each, compared with an issue price of HK$1.07.
Brokers said late short-term buying boosted the shares to a high of HK$1.20 from a low of HK$1.01. Volume was 33.57 million shares worth HK$36.81 million.

"It performed better that we expected in late trade," said one analyst at a local brokerage. "Short-term investors were seen buying the shares on expectation of room on the upside as selling orders diminished in late trade."
Analysts generally expected a weak debut due to the cool response to its initial public offering (IPO) of shares in Hong Kong.
Perennial offered 60 million shares, consisting of 40 million new shares and 20 million existing shares, at HK$1.07 each. Its IPO was about 2.03 times subscribed.
Brokers said they expected profit-taking to pressure the share price in the short run before consolidation.
Perennial said proceeds would be used to boost production capacity, buy machinery, repay debt as well as for working capital.
